hypotheses.title: Persistent potential-field saddle connectors (rtp b2 + Bouguer b13, depth b15 concordance)
hypotheses.signature: Multi-scale Hessian saddle persistence: sqrt(-det H) with opposite-sign eigenvalues at sigma=1 and 3 px, gated by low gradient magnitude; geometric-mean across rtp/gravity, depth-to-basement saddle as concordance multiplier
hypotheses.why_uncatalogued: A buried fault connecting two basement blocks creates a saddle corridor between anomaly highs/lows without a surface scarp or isolated ridge crest, so catalogue traces (mapped where scarps exist) miss it; saddle topology is not a ridge/edge amplitude
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: No prior lane used Hessian-determinant saddle topology/persistence; prior lanes used gradient ridges, phase congruency (H86J-MPC/MCSP), cross-spectral admittance (CSGD), Euler, scarps
hypotheses.mimic: Intrusive lithologic contacts and erosional basement relief creating superposed-source saddles
